page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 physical cores and built on the Nitro hypervisor platform. The system provides 192 dedicated single-threaded physical cores running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz, supported by 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 768.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per core. The server integrates 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and offers 50 Gbps baseline networking throughput.

Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier multi-threaded compute and data processing capabilities. Multi-core execution scores in stress-ng reach 314,716.23, placing the server in the top decile, accompanied by high throughput in Clang software compilation and PassMark database operations. Memory subsystem performance is strong, registering 895.14 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 425.78 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB memory blocks. In-memory storage tests show 364.75 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. In contrast, single-core metrics fall within average ranges, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1,643.39 and Geekbench single-core at 1,649.0.

Hardware tradeoffs center around architecture and accelerator support. The arm64 CPU foundation offers significant resource density and cost efficiency for parallelized enterprise tasks, delivering lower operational overhead relative to x86 equivalents. However, the system lacks discrete GPU hardware, which leads to weak performance in large language model inference tasks compared to accelerated nodes. Furthermore, local storage is ephemeral NVMe SSD instance memory, necessitating application-level persistence strategies. The instance is suited for high-concurrency Redis caching, distributed key-value databases, extensive continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, and large-scale web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.48xlarge is a general-purpose, high-density instance based on the arm64 ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture. Managed via the Nitro hypervisor, the server provides 192 dedicated physical cores running at 2.7 GHz with single-threaded execution per core, paired with 768 GB of system memory at a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Local ephemeral storage consists of 11,400 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, complemented by a 50 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate exceptional throughput across multi-threaded execution, high memory bandwidth, and intensive disk operations, evidenced by top-tier results in Redis transactions, Clang software compilation, and PassMark database operations. Conversely, single-core benchmarks reflect typical mid-range performance, and language model inference remains constrained without dedicated hardware accelerators. With strong multi-core scalability and integrated high-speed local storage, the instance delivers high resource efficiency for distributed databases, caching clusters, large-scale CI/CD build environments, and high-throughput static web serving.
